text:
jen: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a couple of fat-tail capacity questions re: GPU supply, regions, and autoscale. Threading here so we don't overload the Q/A doc.

alex: Thanks Jen. Which fallback order should apps expect when a region runs out? e.g., same-region fallback to different SKU -> different region -> degraded model?

maria: High-level plan: prewarm in-region where possible -> same-region alternate SKU (quantized or lower-memory variant) -> nearby region (latency tradeoff) -> dedicated fallback (reserved capacity) if the customer has a commit. We prefer SKU/regional fallbacks over automatic model downgrades unless customers opt into model fallbacks.

kyle: To add: routing policy evaluation order is capacity_hint -> customer_tier -> latency_slo -> cost_preference. So free-tier/low-commit traffic is more likely to go to cheaper fallbacks earlier.

jen: How do pricing and token accounting change during fallbacks? Some customers asked whether tokens are billed differently if we switch models mid-request.

rebecca: Billing note: charge is based on the model that produced each token. If we switch mid-stream we attribute tokens to the model variant actually used. The billing console will show per-request breakdowns (model, tokens, unit price).

sam: Is there a graceful degradation path so responses aren't abruptly truncated/hallucination-prone when we switch models? That's a common concern.

maria: Yes — whenever possible we do KV/prefix cache transfer across compatible families. For incompatible families we perform a "continuation handoff": we include a short system-level prompt like `/* context continuation: bridge from model A to model B, re-generate up to N tokens for coherency */` and mark the response metadata so clients can surface it. We also set conservative sampling settings on the fallback model to reduce divergence.

kyle: Example (internal) routing snippet for clarity:
```
policy:
  prewarm_region: true
  sku_order: [v100-32g, a100-40g, t4-16g]
  model_fallback: [redwood-2-small, redwood-2-base]
  latency_threshold_ms: 120
```

tia: Will we publish metrics after a big spike (e.g., % of requests routed to fallbacks, median latency delta)? Customers asked for transparency.

alex: Yes — for any incident-sized spike we'll publish a short summary with: percent affected, time-in-fallback distribution, median latency change, and a link to the ops runbook and postmortem. Non-sensitive telemetry only.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary config for region-fallback policy updated by @kyle at 16:42 — rollout moved from 20% to 50%.

jen: Action items: kyle to add a public FAQ blurb about billing and fallbacks; maria to draft an internal doc on handoff semantics and sampling defaults; rebecca to confirm billing UI surfaces per-model token splits. I'll sync with comms about a short customer note.

kyle: :thumbsup: I'll get a PR up by EOD and add a blurb in the release notes.

rebecca: :raised_hands: Confirming UI change is scoped for next release, will share tracking ticket shortly.

jen: Thanks all — if anyone else has customer-facing questions, drop them here and we'll fold into the FAQ.
